articles.title: Obsession takeover: A Rs 7 crore horror film just exposed Bollywood’s biggest issue - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: A low-budget horror film, "Obsession," directed by Curry Barker and starring Michael Johnston and Inde Navarrette, has become Hollywood's biggest ROI story of 2026.  The film, made for a reported budget of $750,000 to $1 million (roughly Rs 6–8 crore), grossed over $100 million worldwide, earning nearly 80 to 100 times its production cost. This success highlights the shrinking space for mid-budget theatrical films in Bollywood, where studios increasingly prioritize large-scale spectacles and franchise universes.  The film's low-risk, high-concept storytelling model contrasts with the escalating budgets of recent blockbuster releases like "RRR" and "Dhurandhar: The Revenge," which have also achieved significant box office success but rely on massive production costs.

articles.title: Rajat Patidar and Shubman Gill talk T20I selection chances before IPL 2026 final. And it’s not straightforward responses - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Rajat Patidar and Shubman Gill, captains of their respective teams in the IPL final, have provided insights into their T20I selection prospects. Both players have delivered impressive performances this season, with Patidar's explosive innings against Gujarat Titans and Gill's consistent scoring across formats. The outcome of the final will significantly impact their chances for a spot in the upcoming T20I series against Ireland and England.  The selectors will meet shortly after the game to finalize the squad.

articles.title: Hantavirus Quarantine to End for Some US Cruise Passengers | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is monitoring 18 Americans at the University of Nebraska Medical Center’s National Quarantine Unit in Omaha for hantavirus symptoms.  Two New Yorkers are expected to be released from isolation next week, while another will remain in Nebraska until June 22nd. The remaining passengers' details haven't been released. The CDC continues to work with state and local health departments during the 42-day monitoring period.

articles.title: INDIA Bloc Revival In Bengal? Support For Mamata Banerjee Over Nephew's Assault
articles.rephrased_article: Despite losing the Bengal election, Mamata Banerjee's stature within the INDIA bloc remains strong. Opposition leaders condemned the assault on her nephew, Abhishek Banerjee, by a mob in Sonarpur, South 24 Parganas.  Mallikarjun Kharge, Akhilesh Yadav, and Arvind Kejriwal accused the BJP of fostering political violence, while the ruling party denied involvement and blamed the TMC for mischaracterizing public anger. The incident has led to calls for stronger law-and-order measures in West Bengal.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Political violence against a prominent politician is a serious concern.

articles.title: No Ambulance Or Doctor In Jammu And Kashmir Village, Pregnant Woman Carried On Shoulders, Baby Dies
articles.rephrased_article: A pregnant woman, Shaista Begum, lost her baby in the mountainous Kishtwar district of Jammu and Kashmir after a difficult journey to medical care.  Her family carried her for miles due to lack of roads and ambulances before reaching a primary health center with no gynaecologist on duty. The family then embarked on a 120-kilometer journey to the Government Medical College in Anantnag, where the baby died during the journey. Villagers are demanding improved healthcare facilities in Marwah, including a gynaecologist and a 24-hour ambulance.

articles.title: Punjab civic polls: Early edge to Congress as counting proceeds amid tight security - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Congress is surging ahead in the early stages of counting for Punjab's civic body elections, with strong performances in several municipal wards.  The counting process began on Friday amidst heavy security deployment at multiple counting centers across the state. The AAP, BJP, and SAD are also contesting the elections, which are being viewed as a key indicator of the political mood ahead of next year's Assembly elections. A total of 7,555 candidates contested the election, with Congress leading in several wards.  The outcome is expected to serve as an important indicator of the political mood in Punjab ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.

articles.title: 'Enhancing Capabilities For China, Pakistan's 2-Front Challenge': Navy Chief
articles.rephrased_article: The Indian Navy has enhanced its anti-submarine warfare capabilities, underwater surveillance, and network-centric operations to counter potential threats from China and Pakistan.  Admiral Dinesh K Tripathi, the Navy Chief, stated that these efforts are not directed at any specific nation but aim to secure India's maritime interests. The Indian Navy is focusing on credible deterrence through technological integration, sustained presence, and operational readiness, including the acquisition of six stealth submarines under Project 75(I).  The Navy is also committed to achieving self-reliance in defense by building its own platforms and industrial capabilities.

articles.title: Congress’s message to Siddaramaiah as DKS takes charge: Won’t allow you to rest - Karnataka News | India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Congress general secretary KC Venugopal declared that the party will not allow former Karnataka Chief Minister Siddaramaiah to rest, urging him to continue playing an active role in both state and national politics.  After Siddaramaiah's resignation, DK Shivakumar was unanimously elected as the new CLP leader and formally named Karnataka’s next Chief Minister.  Siddaramaiah congratulated Shivakumar and called for a "second freedom struggle" to protect the country's unity and integrity. The Congress leadership expressed confidence that under Shivakumar's leadership, they will return to power in the 2028 elections.

articles.title: SF Campaign: Andhra has more obese men among large states, Kerala tops among women - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: The National Family Health Survey-6 (NFHS-6) revealed that Andhra Pradesh has the highest prevalence of overweight or obese men among large Indian states, with 47.9% of men aged 15 to 49 years classified as such.  Kerala leads in female obesity prevalence, with 46.7% of women in that age group classified as overweight or obese. The survey highlights a growing obesity burden across southern states, with rising prevalence in both urban and rural areas, raising concerns over lifestyle-related diseases. Public health experts have warned that obesity is becoming a widespread challenge across rural India as well.

articles.title: Donald Trump’s daughter visits Taj Mahal
articles.rephrased_article: Tiffany Trump, daughter of Donald Trump, visited the Taj Mahal with her husband, Michael Boulos, on Saturday.  She toured the monument extensively and expressed interest in its history and architecture. Security was heightened for the visit, with a high-security corridor established from the airport to the Taj Mahal. After leaving the monument, she returned to her hotel with Boulos and will continue their India trip.

articles.title: Vinesh Phogat’s return to wrestling: What a mess - India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Vinesh Phogat, one of India's greatest-ever wrestlers, returned to the wrestling mat in a bid to qualify for the 2026 Asian Games. However, her comeback was marred by conflict with the Wrestling Federation of India (WFI), which imposed restrictions on her weight class and created an atmosphere of tension throughout the competition. Despite facing challenges like being denied entry into the stadium and experiencing biased officiating, Phogat persevered but ultimately lost in the semi-final. The WFI's actions sparked outrage from fans and athletes alike, highlighting a systemic issue within the federation that needs to be addressed.

articles.title: US Aircraft Fires Missile At Gambia flagged Ship For Iran Blockade Violation
articles.rephrased_article: US Central Command (CENTCOM) disabled a Gambia-flagged cargo ship, the M/V Lian Star, attempting to sail to an Iranian port by firing a Hellfire missile into its engine room on May 29. The strike followed over 20 warnings issued to the vessel's crew, who failed to comply.  The ship is no longer transiting to Iran and the US has disabled five commercial vessels in an effort to enforce a blockade of Iranian ports as part of a ceasefire with Tehran.

articles.title: 'Dhobi' on mortuary duty: HR crisis dogs busy medical college in Kerala - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: The Government Medical College (GMC), Manjeri, is facing severe staffing shortages despite its growing role as a major tertiary-care teaching hospital.  Malappuram, with its unprecedented political influence in the new UDF government, has sparked hopes that long-pending issues at the medical college will be addressed. The institution struggles with chronic staff shortages, vacant specialist posts, and administrative bottlenecks, leading to employees taking on responsibilities far beyond their designated roles. The GMC faces a shortage of 271 permanent positions and 32 vacancies under the Health Department.  A study conducted by the Personnel and Administrative Reforms Department revealed that outsourced workers are handling crucial duties due to staff shortages, highlighting the urgent need for additional personnel. The institution recommends converting all 40 outsourced posts into permanent ones and creating six new posts to address the growing workload.

articles.title: Audit of fundamental rights’ effectiveness could yield ‘uncomfortable’ findings: J. Chelameswar - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: J. Chelameswar, former Supreme Court judge, expressed concerns about the effectiveness of constitutional rights in protecting common people during a conference on legal education. He suggested an audit could reveal "very uncomfortable" findings and emphasized that the system's progress should be examined by the judicial fraternity. K. Chandru, former judge of the Madras High Court, also spoke at the event, questioning the need for an "Indianised jurisprudence" while advocating for legal studies to address contemporary issues like poverty and caste.

articles.title: Naga Chaitanya Approaches Delhi HC Over Defamatory Content Alleging He Cheated On Samantha | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Naga Chaitanya, an actor, has filed a petition in the Delhi High Court against online content and defamatory claims alleging he cheated on his ex-wife Samantha Ruth Prabhu. The actor's legal team argues that unauthorized use of his name, image, and persona across various platforms is damaging his reputation.  Justice Jyoti Singh acknowledged the vulnerability of public figures but stressed limitations to scrutiny. The court will examine Chaitanya's plea for legal protections against such online misuse.

articles.title: Abhishek Banerjee Sonarpur attack: TMC leader alleges BJP wanted to kill him; shirt torn, specs broken, Stones, eggs and 'chor chor' chants - West Bengal News | India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, TMC national general secretary, was attacked by a mob in Sonarpur, West Bengal while visiting the family of a man allegedly killed in post-poll violence. The incident involved stones, eggs, and verbal abuse, with protesters accusing him of corruption and demanding security for the area. Mamata Banerjee, Chief Minister of West Bengal, visited him at the hospital and blamed the BJP for orchestrating the attack.  Derek O'Brien, a Trinamool Congress Rajya Sabha MP, questioned the withdrawal of security during the visit and called for an investigation. The BJP condemned the violence but denied any involvement in the attack.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Political violence against a high-ranking official is a serious threat to democracy.

articles.title: LG directs Ladakh Admin to adopt austerity measures as per PM's call
articles.rephrased_article: Vinai Kumar Saxena, the Lieutenant Governor of Ladakh, has issued directives to all departments to promote austerity and sustainable practices in line with Prime Minister Narendra Modi's call for a greener future. Saxena directed departments to reduce government expenditure, cut fuel consumption, promote renewable energy, encourage local products, and enhance environmental sustainability. He also emphasized the need for greater domestic tourism, natural farming, and efficient resource utilization across sectors. All departments have been asked to submit an action plan report within 30 days and launch public awareness campaigns on various sustainable initiatives.

articles.title: Indian student drowned at Wisconsin dam as he jumped to save three friends; feet got stuck in fishing wire - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Anurup Reddy Koduru, a 22-year-old Indian student who recently graduated from the University of North Texas, drowned at Toledo Bend Reservoir on May 29th.  He was swimming with friends when he became entangled in fishing wire and was pulled under water. The incident involved multiple agencies including the South Sabine Fire District, LA Department of Wildlife and Fisheries, North Sabine Fire District, Sabine River Authority, Acadian Ambulance, Life Air Rescue, and the Sabine Parish Sheriff Dive Team. Ashtrith Reddy Koduru, his brother, has set up a fundraiser to help with repatriation and funeral expenses.

articles.title: D K Shivakumar elected Cong Legislature Party leader, set to be new Karnataka CM
articles.rephrased_article: D K Shivakumar was elected leader of the legislature party in Karnataka, paving the way for him to become the state's next chief minister.  Siddaramaiah, the outgoing chief minister, proposed Shivakumar's name and the meeting unanimously endorsed it.  The CLP meeting took a ten-minute break with top leaders including Siddaramaiah, KC Venugopal, and Randeep Singh Surjewala in a separate room.  Shivakumar will be sworn in as the new CM on June 3rd.

articles.title: Six dalits hacked over banner dispute in Tenkasi; Residents protest seeking justice - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: A masked gang attacked six members of the Devendra Kula Vellalar community in Tenkasi district, Tamil Nadu, on May 29th during a wedding celebration. The victims sustained severe injuries and were hospitalized.  P. Uchimakali, CPI(M) Tenkasi district secretary, claims the attack was caste-driven and stems from a dispute over a banner erected for the wedding. Police have detained eight individuals in connection with the incident, including three juveniles. Investigations are ongoing.

articles.title: Ukraine Is Using Soldiers That Don't Need Food Or Water To Kill Russians
articles.rephrased_article: Ukraine's war effort is increasingly reliant on drones and robots, replacing traditional frontline soldiers.  These unmanned systems are used for attacks, reconnaissance, and even medical evacuation, with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky highlighting the success of using them to capture Russian positions. The use of these machines has been accelerated by a manpower shortage and uncertainty over Western support, giving Ukraine a technological advantage against a larger Russian force.  The rapid adoption of this technology is transforming warfare, as seen in the nickname "silent death" given to robotic bomb carriers by captured Russian soldiers.

articles.title: From blacklisting clauses to technical criteria: Class 12 student exposes Coempt Eduteck tender - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: A 12th-grade student, Sarthak Sidhant, alleges that the Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE) revised tender conditions to favor Coempt Eduteck, a company with a history of operational failures.  The changes included removing disqualification provisions for past performance issues and lowering turnover requirements.  Sidhant claims these alterations allowed Coempt to qualify despite its previous track record and benefited from other modifications like relaxed software ownership requirements and penalties related to delivery timelines.  Rahul Gandhi has demanded an independent judicial inquiry, while KTR, former Telangana Minister, criticized the CBSE's actions and called for accountability from the Union Government.

articles.title: Short: Indian Navy confined entire Pak Navy to its ports during Operation Sindoor: Rajnath
articles.rephrased_article: Defence Minister Rajnath Singh inaugurated the 'Nausena Shaurya Vatika', an open-air naval museum in Lucknow, highlighting India's maritime security and advancements in defence manufacturing. The museum showcases the Indian Navy's legacy, operational capabilities, and achievements, including the decommissioned warship INS Gomati. Singh emphasized the importance of maritime security for national well-being and praised Uttar Pradesh's economic growth under Chief Minister Yogi Adityanath.  The museum aims to inspire future generations and educate the public about the value of freedom and security.

articles.title: Is the war in Ukraine entering a new phase? | Russia-Ukraine war News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A drone attack on a building in Romania, blamed by Romanian President Nicusor Dan on Russia, has reignited concerns about the war's escalation.  NATO stated it is prepared to defend its territory against attacks, while Russian President Vladimir Putin denied responsibility and claimed the war was nearing an end. Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy warned of a major aerial assault planned by Russia. The incident has raised questions about the potential for NATO involvement in the conflict.

articles.title: Assault On Abhishek Banerjee: âPre-Planned Attack By BJP Goonsâ, Alleges Trinamool Congress | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Opposition parties, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge and Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav, condemned the assault on TMC leader Abhishek Banerjee in West Bengal's Sonarpur, blaming the BJP.  They accused the ruling party of orchestrating a "murderous attack" and using violence to silence opposition voices. The incident prompted calls for increased security for all Opposition leaders and an end to political violence.  The BJP, however, denied involvement and claimed the attack was a manifestation of public anger against the ruling Trinamool Congress.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Allegations of a politically motivated assault raise concerns about violence and suppression of opposition.

articles.title: DK Shivakumar elected CLP chief, to take charge as Karnataka CM on 3 June - The South First | News, Politics, Sports, Entertainment & Live Updates
articles.rephrased_article: DK Shivakumar was invited by Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot to take the oath of office as Karnataka's 18th Chief Minister.  The Congress Legislature Party (CLP) unanimously elected Shivakumar as its leader on May 30, after he staked a claim to form the government and moved a resolution thanking former Chief Minister Siddaramaiah for his service. Surjewala and Venugopal, AICC general secretaries, attended the CLP meeting at the Vidhana Soudha.

articles.title: Trump hits out at federal judge for blocking Kennedy Center's renovation closure; slams US court system | Today News
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump criticized District Judge Christopher Cooper's ruling that blocked the renovation of the Kennedy Center, calling him an "anti-Trump hater" and predicting its closure.  The judge ordered the removal of Trump's name from the center, citing Congressional authority over the institution's name. Trump claimed the board added his name to the center for strategic reasons and vowed to relinquish control of the Kennedy Center to Congress. He also expressed frustration with the Supreme Court’s rejection of his tariffs and suggested a rigged court system.

articles.title: How Municipal Poll Setback Brought Congress Factionalism To Fore In Punjab
articles.rephrased_article: The Congress suffered a disappointing performance in the Punjab municipal elections, losing to the ruling Aam Aadmi Party. This setback has reignited concerns about leadership within the party and fueled internal power struggles. Several senior leaders are positioning themselves for key organizational roles ahead of the 2027 Assembly elections.  While the high command has stated there will be no immediate organizational changes, factionalism remains a significant challenge for the party as it seeks to address accountability and build unity for future electoral success.

articles.title: âHe Chose Service Over Stardomâ: Ram Charan Hails Tamil Nadu CM Vijay | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: Ram Charan, actor, praised Vijay, Tamil Nadu Chief Minister, for stepping away from his successful film career to serve the people.  He expressed pride in Vijay and congratulated both the people of Tamil Nadu and Vijay.  The political party TVK, led by Vijay, secured a majority in the Tamil Nadu Assembly after garnering support from other parties.

articles.title: 'It's like a decaying body': Australia farmers battle mouse plague
articles.rephrased_article: Farmers across Australia are battling a severe mouse plague, which has caused significant damage to crops and homes.  The CSIRO, a national science agency, estimates that mouse populations in some areas have reached thousands per hectare. The situation is exacerbated by rising fuel and fertilizer costs due to the ongoing US-Israeli war on Iran.  Farmers are spending large sums of money on baiting and replanting crops as they struggle with the unprecedented scale of the infestation. Belinda Eastough, an agronomist, reports that mice have been particularly abundant in paddocks where a bumper harvest has provided ample food sources. While cooler temperatures and the availability of stronger bait offer some hope for relief, farmers remain concerned about the long-term impact of this plague on their livelihoods.

articles.title: Abhishek Banerjee Sonarpur attack: TMC leader alleges BJP wanted to kill him; shirt torn, specs broken, Stones, eggs and 'chor chor' chants - West Bengal News | India Today
articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, Trinamool Congress national general secretary, was attacked by a mob in Sonarpur, West Bengal, while visiting the family of a man allegedly killed in post-poll violence. The incident involved stones, eggs, and verbal abuse directed at Banerjee, who sustained injuries to his shirt and spectacles. Mamata Banerjee, Chief Minister of West Bengal, visited him at the hospital and accused the BJP of orchestrating the attack. The BJP denied involvement but condemned the violence, while Derek O'Brien, a Trinamool Congress Rajya Sabha MP, questioned the security arrangements.  The incident has escalated tensions between the ruling party and the opposition, with accusations of political vendetta and attempts to intimidate prominent figures.
articles.civic_flag_reason: Political violence against a high-ranking official raises concerns about safety and rule of law.

The incident involved multiple agencies including the South Sabine Fire District, LA Department of Wildlife and Fisheries, North Sabine Fire District, Sabine River Authority, Acadian Ambulance, Life Air Rescue, and Sabine Parish Sheriff Dive Team.

articles.title: Div Com Kashmir reviews Amarnath Yatra arrangements in Pahalgam
articles.rephrased_article: Anshul Garg, Divisional Commissioner of Kashmir, conducted a review meeting in Pahalgam to assess preparations for the upcoming Shri Amarnath Ji Yatra-2026. The meeting involved representatives from various departments including the Jal Shakti Department, KPDCL, BRO, Health Department, Municipal authorities, Fire and Emergency Services, and telecom service providers.  Garg directed departments to ensure uninterrupted water supply, power supply, road maintenance, healthcare facilities, sanitation measures, communication services, and RFID card issuance for service providers. He also emphasized the importance of inter-departmental coordination and close collaboration with stakeholders.

articles.title: Kochi sailor who endured Equatorial Guinea’s detention feels relieved with international tribunal’s verdict - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea
articles.rephrased_article: Sanu Jose, a sailor from Kerala, India, and the chief officer of the cargo ship MT Heroic Idun, welcomed the International Tribunal for the Law of the Sea (ITLOS) ruling against Equatorial Guinea over the detention of the vessel in 2022. The verdict awarded more than $14 million to the Marshall Islands, where the ship was registered, and found Equatorial Guinea had violated UNCLOS by intercepting and detaining the crew. This is the largest amount ever awarded by ITLOS.  The ruling has brought relief to Mr. Jose and other sailors who were detained, providing confidence in the maritime community.

articles.title: Many Feared Trapped As 5-Storeyed Building Collapses Near Metro Station In South Delhi | OdishaBytes
articles.rephrased_article: A five-storey building collapsed in south Delhi's Mehrauli area on Saturday evening, trapping dozens of people under the debris. Rescue teams are working to locate survivors and have so far extricated four individuals alive.  The cause of the collapse is still unknown, but authorities believe it was triggered by a dust storm that swept across Delhi-NCR earlier in the day. Delhi Fire Service personnel responded quickly, calling for reinforcements and cordoning off the area to facilitate rescue efforts.

articles.title: PSG beat Arsenal to win back-to-back Champions League titles after shootout | Football News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: PSG defeated Arsenal 4-3 on penalties after a 1-1 draw in extra time to win back-to-back Champions League titles.  The French side, under coach Luis Enrique, overcame a strong Arsenal defense and capitalized on their opportunities in the shootout. Declan Rice was devastated by the loss but proud of his team's performance throughout the season.

articles.title: Ecuador accused of meddling in Colombian election with tariff vow
articles.rephrased_article: Ecuador's president, Daniel Noboa, has accused Colombia's presidential candidate Abelardo de la Espriella of accepting a "goodwill measure" to lift tariffs in exchange for handing over criminals.  The Colombian foreign ministry condemned this as interference in their democratic process and threatened national sovereignty. The upcoming election is expected to redefine Colombia's political alliances, particularly regarding its stance on drug trafficking and security.

articles.title: Building collapses near Saket metro station; 8 persons rescued, several feared trapped - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: An eight-story building collapsed in Saket, Delhi on Saturday evening, trapping several people under the debris. Delhi Fire Services officials responded to the scene and rescued at least eight individuals.  The incident occurred near a tin shed canteen where children were dining, creating panic and prompting a large-scale rescue operation involving multiple agencies including National Disaster Response Force, Delhi Police, and District Disaster Management Authority.

articles.title: Malls, e-commerce hit school accessories market hard - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Traders in the school market are experiencing a decline in sales as students and parents tighten their budgets due to rising prices and economic concerns. Rajesh A.G., an autorickshaw driver, and Sumesh, a parent, report increased financial strain on their families.  Althaf Ismail and Abdul Razak, owners of stationery stores, have seen sales drop as students prefer online shopping for school supplies.

articles.title: Iran reasserts control over Hormuz Strait as deal with US remains elusive | US-Israel war on Iran News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Iran has reasserted control over the Strait of Hormuz, warning foreign vessels to comply with regulations or face consequences. The Pentagon chief stated that the US is prepared to restart war if a satisfactory deal isn't reached. While President Donald Trump met with advisors and indicated a "final determination" on a potential deal, no statement followed the meeting.  Iran’s Foreign Ministry spokesperson denied an agreement was reached, while Iranian officials accused the US of “betraying diplomacy” by continuing the naval blockade.

articles.title: Kanye West concert in Italy cancelled over ‘public order and safety issues’ | Kanye West | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Kanye West's concert in Italy has been cancelled due to public order and safety concerns, following a meeting with local authorities. The decision was made after the Prefect of Reggio Emilia, Salvatore Angieri, received concerns from the local Jewish community regarding West's past antisemitic remarks.  A similar cancellation occurred for fellow US rapper Travis Scott at the Hellwatt festival due to scheduling conflicts and safety concerns following a previous tragedy at his Astroworld festival in Houston, Texas.

articles.title: ‘Red alert’ in Bengaluru: City gripped by IPL final fever as RCB looks for second consecutive win - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Royal Challengers Bengaluru (RCB) will face the Gujarat Titans in a high-stakes Indian Premier League (IPL) final on Sunday, with celebrations already underway in Bengaluru.  Fans are donning red attire and streets are filled with vendors selling merchandise. Major pubs and restaurants are also experiencing early bookings for the match.

articles.title: RFP to be floated for Amaravati Economic Region development plan - The Hindu
articles.sentiment_target: Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA)
articles.rephrased_article: The Andhra Pradesh Capital Region Development Authority (APCRDA) approved a development plan for the Amaravati Economic Region, which spans nine districts. The meeting also saw decisions to create a special tribunal for building disputes and allocate funds for the Andhra Pradesh High Court buildings. Additionally, the APCRDA authorized a City Gas Distribution network in PPP models and land allotments for unsuitable plots under the Negotiable Settlement Policy.

articles.title: 'Bringing the war back where it came from': Zelenskyy after Ukrainian drones hit Russian oil facilities - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Ukrainian drone strikes damaged oil facilities in Russia's Rostov and Krasnodar regions, according to Russian officials. Zelenskyy confirmed the attack on an oil depot in Armavir, highlighting Ukraine's growing ability to target deep inside Russian territory.  The attacks come as Ukraine continues to expand its long-range strike capabilities against Russian energy infrastructure, while Russia has also intensified attacks on Ukrainian cities and energy facilities.

articles.title: Tangedco replaces electrical poles damaged by strong winds in Tiruvannamalai - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Tangedco replaced 55 damaged electrical poles in Kannamangalam and surrounding farming villages due to strong winds, aiming to prevent power interruptions. The damage occurred in areas with frequent evening rain and strong winds that affected agricultural lands and village roads.  The replacement effort was completed within five days, according to Tangedco officials.  This action aims to ensure uninterrupted power supply for the 45,000 consumers served by Kannamangalam substation.

articles.title: Ebola Outbreak: 'We’re with you': WHO chief rushes to Congo as Ebola outbreak worsens - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: World Health Organisation Director-General Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus visited the Democratic Republic of Congo to address a rapidly spreading Ebola outbreak. He urged stronger international support, including increased funding and community engagement, emphasizing that local cooperation is crucial for controlling the virus.  Tedros stressed the importance of addressing misinformation and mistrust surrounding the response, while also calling on countries with travel restrictions to reconsider them. The outbreak has already spread across three eastern DRC provinces and into neighboring Uganda, with at least 1,077 suspected cases and 246 deaths reported in the DRC. Doctors Without Borders warned that the response is struggling to keep pace with the outbreak’s rapid spread.

articles.title: State Highways opens new bridge near government hospital in Walajah - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: State Highways officials opened a new ₹15.20 crore bridge near the Government Taluk Hospital in Walajah town to improve safety for hospital staff and students crossing the busy Walajah-Sholinghur High Road. The two-lane, 500-meter-long bridge features LED streetlights, tiled footpaths with steel hand railings, and a service lane.  Work on stormwater drains, LED streetlights, and road safety measures is ongoing and expected to be completed in the coming weeks.

articles.title: Trump attacks artists dropping out of US Freedom 250 concert and mulls appearing himself
articles.rephrased_article: Donald Trump has expressed interest in holding a rally at the same time and location as the Freedom 250 event, which celebrates America's 250th birthday.  Several artists, including Young MC, Morris Day, The Commodores, Poison frontman Bret Michaels, and Martina McBride, have withdrawn from the festival citing political motivations. While rappers Flo Rida and Vanilla Ice are still scheduled to perform, Freedom 250 maintains that the event is non-partisan. Spokeswoman Rachel Reisner stated that the organization aims to welcome all Americans to the fair.

articles.title: Who has to leave US for Green Card and who doesn't: New USCIS rule, clarification explained - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: USCIS and the Department of Homeland Security have clarified their stance on Green Card applications, stating that most immigrants will remain in the US while their applications are processed.  The initial announcement had sparked concerns among industries, but the clarification suggests it was not a significant policy change. However, experts remain uncertain about the exact implications of this new guidance, as it leaves room for individual discretion by immigration officers regarding Green Card applicants' residency status.

articles.title: Minister inaugurates Katpadi MLA office in Vellore - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: V. Gandhiraj, Tamil Nadu Minister of Co-operatives, inaugurated the refurbished MLA office for Katpadi Assembly constituency in Vellore. The 950 sq ft facility, built in 2001 on a government plot, includes a separate chamber for incumbent M. Sudhakar of the Tamilaga Vettri Kazhagam (TVK), an office room, record room, and a waiting hall accommodating up to 50-60 people. The renovated office also features parking facilities, washrooms, and drinking water.

articles.title: Marcia Lucas: Oscar-winning Star Wars editor dies aged 80
articles.rephrased_article: Marcia Lucas, the Oscar-winning editor of the original Star Wars film, has died at 80 from metastatic cancer.  She was married to George Lucas, the creator of the franchise, and worked on several of his films including *THX 1138* and *American Graffiti*.  Lucas won an Academy Award for Best Film Editing in 1977 for *A New Hope*, and also collaborated with directors like Martin Scorsese on acclaimed films. Her family described her as a "trailblazer" who helped redefine film editing, leaving behind a legacy of emotional intelligence and impactful storytelling.

articles.title: Palestinian doctor killed, three people injured in Israeli attack on Gaza | Israel-Palestine conflict News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: A Palestinian doctor, Dr. Jamal Abu Aboun, was killed and three people injured in an Israeli attack on central Gaza.  Israeli settlers also attacked Palestinian homes and property across the occupied West Bank, including Beita and Khirbet el-Muraq. Israel launched its genocidal war on Gaza in October 2023, resulting in at least 72,000 Palestinian deaths and over 172,000 injuries, according to Palestinian figures.  The attacks come amid continued Israeli violations of a United States-backed ceasefire aimed at halting the conflict.

articles.title: US says it is 'more than capable' of resume war with Iran as talks remain unresolved - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: President Donald Trump has stated that any agreement with Iran must meet key US conditions, including a permanent end to Iran's nuclear weapons ambitions. A draft framework is awaiting Trump's approval but he has not yet made a decision.  US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth emphasized the US military readiness to restart operations if necessary, while CENTCOM reiterated American forces' presence in the region. Diplomatic efforts continue despite conflicting signals over a potential breakthrough. Tensions remain high, with Iran accusing the US of dictating terms and continuing to block access to the Strait of Hormuz.  The situation is further complicated by ongoing fighting in Lebanon between Israel and Hezbollah.

articles.title: Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple panel demands action against cops for submitting ‘false’ report - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Sree Padmanabha Swamy Temple management committee has requested the State government to take action against police officers who submitted a report alleging missing gold and security lapses without conducting proper inquiries. The report, based on intelligence information, claimed thefts of valuables and breaches at the temple. However, the temple management committee refuted these allegations, stating that the missing items were found inside the sanctum sanctorum and that the security checks were in place.

articles.title: EU's top diplomat Kallas to visit Islamabad on June 1 for strategic dialogue - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Kaja Kallas, EU High Representative for Foreign Affairs and Security Policy, will visit Pakistan on June 1st to participate in the 8th EU-Pakistan Strategic Dialogue.  She will meet with President Asif Ali Zardari, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif, and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir. The dialogue aims to discuss bilateral relations under the Strategic Engagement Plan signed in 2019. The EU is Pakistan's second-largest trading partner, with GSP+ status allowing duty-free or minimum duty on European exports.  The EU has commended Pakistan's progress towards implementing international conventions under the GSP+ framework but also highlighted areas for improvement.

articles.title: 'No-one feels safe now': Residents of Romanian city hit by drone share fears
articles.rephrased_article: Romania's residents are expressing fear after a drone attack on an apartment building in Galati, injuring several people. The incident occurred early Friday morning as dozens of residents slept, sparking a fire and panic. President Nicosur Dan confirmed the drone was Russian-made, a Geran-2 (Shahed), used to target Ukrainian ports. While Romania's government has condemned Russia's actions and called for increased military support from NATO, they have not invoked Article 5 of the treaty or expelled the Russian ambassador.  The incident highlights the escalating threat of drone attacks in Europe, with similar incidents occurring in Ukraine.

articles.title: Mob attacks Trinamool leader Abhishek Banerjee; Mamata blames it on BJP - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Abhishek Banerjee, general secretary of the Trinamool Congress, was attacked by a mob in Sonarpur, West Bengal on Saturday. The attack occurred during his visit to the residence of a party worker allegedly killed in post-poll violence.  The mob threw eggs and shoes at Banerjee as security personnel attempted to shield him from the crowd chanting "chor chor" (thief thief).
articles.civic_flag_reason: Political violence against a party leader raises concerns about safety and rule of law.

articles.title: West Bengal Cabinet expansion on June 1 - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Suvendu Adhikari, the West Bengal Chief Minister, is expected to expand his Cabinet on June 1st and allocate key portfolios to senior BJP leaders. The first BJP Cabinet in the state will likely have over 30 members, with names announced after approval from the party's central leadership.  The selection criteria for the new ministers will consider seniority, regional representation, and experience, aiming to ensure inclusion of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes, women, and representatives from northern and south western Bengal. The Cabinet expansion follows Adhikari's recent swearing-in as a Minister and his oversight of 42 state departments.

articles.title: Senior Sri Lankan monk suspended over child sex abuse allegation | Crime News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pallegama Hemarathana, a senior Sri Lankan monk, has been suspended from his duties after being accused of sexually abusing an 11-year-old girl in 2022. The Council of Monks of the Malwatte Chapter took this rare disciplinary action following police arrest on May 9th. Hemarathana was detained at a private hospital in Colombo while awaiting legal proceedings.  The temple, where the alleged abuse occurred, draws thousands of visitors daily and is considered sacred to Buddhists.

articles.title: Defence Minister inaugurates ‘Nausena Shaurya Vatika’ in Lucknow - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajnath Singh, Yogi Adityanath, and others jointly inaugurated the ‘Nausena Shaurya Vatika’, an open-air naval museum in Lucknow, Uttar Pradesh.  The museum is a second phase of the Nausena Shaurya Sangrahalaya, showcasing the Indian Navy's history and valor. Singh praised the Navy's role in Operation Sindoor, highlighting its pressure on Pakistan during the operation. He also commended the progress of Uttar Pradesh under Adityanath, attributing it to strong law and order and a shift from "goonda raj" to a focus on development and investment.

articles.title: Raheem Sterling made to feel ‘worthless’, says close source amid player’s arrest | UK news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Raheem Sterling, a 31-year-old former England international, was arrested on suspicion of driving under the influence of drugs after his Lamborghini collided with barriers on the M3 motorway. Sterling has been experiencing "immeasurable" psychological strain following a difficult couple of years marked by racist abuse and negative media coverage.  A source close to the player described the arrest as highlighting how players deemed "no longer fit for purpose" are treated as disposable, emphasizing that Sterling is innocent until proven guilty.

articles.title: ‘Opposite visions’: What to know about Colombia’s presidential election | Elections News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The upcoming presidential election in Colombia is shaping up to be a contest between two opposing visions for the country's future. Senator Ivan Cepeda, leading the left-wing candidates, has emerged as the frontrunner, promising continuity with President Gustavo Petro’s policies while advocating for a "Total Peace" approach to resolving the country's internal conflict.  The right wing is facing a fractured field of candidates, including Abelardo de la Espriella and Paloma Valencia, who offer contrasting approaches to security and economic issues. De la Espriella advocates for a hardline security model, while Valencia proposes a more moderate approach with increased police presence and pro-business policies. The election will be crucial as it marks the first time Colombia has held a presidential election since its first leftist president took office.

articles.title: D.K. Shivakumar meets Governor Gehlot, stakes claim to form new govt in Karnataka - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: D.K. Shivakumar, the newly elected leader of the Karnataka Pradesh Congress Committee, will be sworn in as Chief Minister on Wednesday, June 3rd at Lok Bhavan. The event is expected to be attended by the central leadership of the party and Governor Thaawarchand Gehlot has invited him to take the oath at 4:05 p.m.  The power transition was overseen by Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, and Sonia Gandhi.  With Cabinet formation still under discussion, speculation remains about whether a full Cabinet will be sworn in and if there will be deputy Chief Ministers.

articles.title: Romania: Residents shaken after Russian drone strike
articles.rephrased_article: A Russian drone strike injured two people in a building near the Romanian-Ukrainian border, prompting fear among residents. Romanian President Nicușor Dan stated that the drone was likely intercepted by Ukrainian air defenses over Kyiv's territory, while Moscow disputed this claim.

articles.title: Cancer jab can eradicate entire tumours in patients, trial shows | Cancer research | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Doctors at the Institute of Cancer Research (ICR) and Johnson & Johnson announced unprecedented results from a trial of their triple-action cancer jab, amivantamab. The injection shrank tumors in more than a third of patients with head and neck or lung cancer who had failed other treatments. Researchers reported that 15 patients saw complete tumor eradication.  The jab targets EGFR and MET pathways, as well as activating the immune system to attack cancer cells.  Prof Kristian Helin, chief executive of ICR, stated that this study demonstrates how new treatments can lead to meaningful advances for patients with limited treatment options.

articles.title: Confirmed Ebola cases nearly double in days as WHO chief visits DR Congo | Ebola News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: WHO director-general Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus visited the epicenter of a deadly Ebola outbreak in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), urging community involvement in combating the disease. Confirmed cases nearly doubled in two days, reaching 225 on Friday, and the outbreak is spreading rapidly through conflict-hit regions. The Africa CDC reports global funding for the response has significantly decreased, while Doctors Without Borders warns that the response has not kept pace with the outbreak's severity.  The WHO is working to assess experimental drugs and a candidate vaccine, and regional countries are on alert, closing borders with DRC.

articles.title: Is Melania Trump an 'alien'? Indian-origin attorney says White House's immigrant-bashing crosses line - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Rahul Reddy, an Indian-origin immigration attorney, criticized the use of the word "alien" by the White House, arguing that it is dehumanizing and fuels negative perceptions.  He pointed out that while the term is legal in immigration law, its usage by the White House creates a narrative that paints lawful immigrants as outsiders. Reddy questioned if Melania Trump, who was born in Slovenia, is also an alien, highlighting the hypocrisy of using such language when the President's own family has a history of immigration.

articles.title: 8 militants killed on second day of security operation in KP's Darra Adamkhel: security sources - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Security forces in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa's Darra Adamkhel area have killed at least eight militants, including two Afghan nationals from the banned Tariq Gidar group of the Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP), during an ongoing operation. The operation, which began on Friday and is still underway, has resulted in a total of 13 militant deaths.  The area has been cordoned off as security forces continue to pursue remaining militants.

articles.title: Ebola spread in DR Congo 'alarming', charity warns, as WHO chief visits worst-hit area
articles.rephrased_article: The World Health Organization (WHO) head, Dr Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, arrived in the Democratic Republic of Congo to assess the Ebola outbreak response.  Médecins Sans Frontières (MSF) has warned that the rapid spread of the virus is alarming, with over 1,000 suspected cases and at least 246 deaths reported. Tedros urged communities to play a larger role in fighting the disease while acknowledging the challenges posed by ongoing conflict.  The outbreak response has been hampered by border closures and delays in sample testing, but efforts are underway to improve diagnosis and treatment.

articles.title: Ponguleti lays stone for integrated sub-registrar office complex at Banjara Hills - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy, Revenue Minister of Andhra Pradesh, laid the foundation stone for an Integrated Sub-Registrar Office complex in Banjara Hills. The project, expected to be completed within a few months, will combine offices from 13 Sub-Registrar units and other related departments under one roof.  The complex is being built by reputed private firms to improve public access and service delivery while generating employment and boosting business activity in the area.

articles.title: Shackled, transferred, mocked: woman, 23, says she gave in to deportation after ‘humiliating’ ICE detention | ICE (US Immigration and Customs Enforcement) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ana María, a 23-year-old woman from South America, was deported back to her native country after being detained by ICE. She experienced inhumane conditions during her detention, including being shackled and subjected to invasive searches.  She was moved between multiple facilities, enduring painful handcuffs and tight chains that constricted her movement and caused physical discomfort. Despite working hard in the US and having a stable life, she was arrested and deported due to anti-immigration crackdowns under the Trump administration. She is now back in South America, anxious and fearful of potential threats.

articles.title: Mushkin Cheruvu freed from encroachments by HYDRAA - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: HYDRAA forces cleared the full tank level (FTL) of Mushkin Cheruvu, a lake in Hyderabad, reducing its size from 52 acres to less than 20 acres.  The operation was prompted by complaints from locals alleging encroachment by an organization responsible for the lake's development under Corporate Social Responsibility. The agency built a bund to create over 35 acres of land upstream but later removed it after discovering that private patta holders had encroached on the FTL, prompting the removal of huts and temporary structures used for garbage segregation. HYDRAA fenced off the FTL to prevent future encroachments.

articles.title: US garbage incinerators are failing to eliminate ‘forever chemical’ air pollution, experts warn | US news | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Public health advocates and independent experts are criticizing a new report from the Minnesota Resources Recovery Association (MRRA) that claims incinerators in Minnesota reduce Pfas emissions by 99.6%. The report, which was commissioned by state regulators, has been met with skepticism due to its incomplete data, misleading language, and failure to conduct proper testing. Critics argue that the report downplays the health risks associated with incinerator emissions, particularly the release of smaller-but-still-toxic Pfas compounds. They point to research suggesting exposure via air is more significant than previously thought and call for stricter regulations and a commitment from Minnesota officials to address the issue.  The MRRA maintains its findings support the safety of incineration while acknowledging some valid points raised by Zero Burn, an advocacy group that opposes incinerators.

articles.title: Animal welfare violations swarm Miami zoo owned by ex-drug kingpin in Tiger King | Miami | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Zoological Wildlife Foundation (ZWF), owned by convicted drug trafficker Mario Tabraue, has been cited for multiple violations of the Animal Welfare Act following botched breeding attempts involving a clouded leopard and a capybara.  The USDA found that the animals were incompatible and injured during an attempt to breed them. The incidents led to the amputation of the female leopard's leg and the death of the capybara. People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals (Peta) has called for the closure of ZWF, citing its history of animal welfare violations.

articles.title: Government prioritises human life and property: Forest Minister Shibu Baby John - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Forest Minister Shibu Baby John stated that the government's priority is protecting human life and property, while also aiming to address human-wildlife conflict.  He announced a 100-day plan to improve communication between the Forest department and local communities, including addressing tiger attacks in Wayanad. The minister highlighted the increasing population of wild elephants and boars as major threats to farmers, emphasizing the need for scientific studies on ecosystem carrying capacity. He also acknowledged the tragic death of a man in an elephant attack near Athirappilly and pledged to investigate potential human negligence contributing to such incidents.

articles.title: Transporters pause operations in Manipur in protest against trucker’s killing - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Transporters in Manipur suspended operations on Saturday, May 30, 2026, protesting the killing of a trucker from West Bengal's Hooghly. The attack on a convoy of food trucks and oil tankers by Kuki militants on National Highway 202 disrupted essential supplies to Imphal and beyond.  The drivers demanded increased security measures and action against the attackers, while Chief Minister Yumnam Khemchand Singh assured the families of the slain driver that their safety is a priority.

articles.title: Chicago-to-Minneapolis United Airlines flight diverted after attempted cockpit breach | United Airlines | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: A United Airlines flight from Chicago to Minneapolis was diverted to Madison, Wisconsin on Friday night after an unruly passenger attempted to breach the cockpit. The FBI and local police responded to the security concern, detaining the passenger who was then taken into custody.  The flight continued its journey to Minneapolis, landing early Saturday morning with no reported injuries among passengers or crew.

articles.title: Truck carrying Afghan returnees from Pakistan flips on highway, killing 18 | Transport News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: An overloaded truck carrying Afghan refugees from Pakistan overturned on a highway in eastern Afghanistan, killing at least 18 people, including many children.  Zabihullah Mujahid, spokesperson for the Taliban government, expressed condolences and said he was “deeply saddened” by the tragedy. The incident occurred near the Surkhakan intersection in Qarghayi district, with authorities attributing it to the driver falling asleep.  At least 30 other passengers were injured, some critically. Emergency services transferred the wounded to medical facilities in neighboring Nangarhar province. The National Disaster Management Authority announced financial assistance for the affected families.

articles.title: Italy bans Kanye West and Trevor Scott concerts in Reggio Emilia
articles.rephrased_article: Kanye West and Travis Scott concerts in Reggio Emilia, Italy have been canceled due to security concerns. The decision was made by the regional prefecture following a request from the local Jewish community and citing factors including previous concert cancellations by West and the risk of counter-demonstrations.  The events were scheduled for July 17th and 18th at the RFC Arena, with Scott facing scrutiny over the Astroworld Festival tragedy in 2021 where ten people died. The cancellation follows West's recent antisemitic comments that led to his ban from entering the UK.

articles.title: Ian McKellen joins march for LGBTQ+ equality in Commonwealth countries | Ian McKellen | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Ian McKellen, joined a demonstration organized by the Peter Tatchell Foundation and the Out and Proud African LGBTI Network in central London to highlight laws criminalizing LGBTQ+ people in 29 Commonwealth countries.  The march, dubbed the “Commonwealth Walk of Shame”, aimed to pressure these nations to repeal such laws, which include life imprisonment or even death penalty in some cases. McKellen emphasized that this demonstration was about love for justice and equality, urging politicians to address this issue more openly. He expressed hope that the event would encourage discussion on the matter within the Commonwealth.

articles.title: Rescuers free four more men from flooded Laos cave, two still missing | Floods News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Rescuers have successfully freed five of the seven men trapped in a flooded cave in central Laos after 10 days. The four men were rescued on Saturday, following a period of near-constant flooding that cut them off from the surface. Two men remain missing as rescue teams continue to search for them deeper within the flooded passages.  The operation involved divers from several countries and faced treacherous conditions with limited visibility in narrow tunnels.

articles.title: Sabalenka, Osaka set up French Open clash, Gauff eyes second week - Sport - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Aryna Sabalenka and Naomi Osaka advanced to the fourth round of the French Open, setting up a blockbuster match-up.  Sabalenka, the top seed, defeated Daria Kasatkina in straight sets while Osaka battled past Iva Jovic. Coco Gauff will attempt to join them in the second week when she takes on Anastasia Potapova.  The men's draw is wide open following the early exits of top seeds Jannik Sinner and Novak Djokovic, with Flavio Cobolli advancing after a victory over Learner Tien.

articles.title: Aukus: US, UK and Australia to develop underwater drone technology
articles.rephrased_article: The US, UK and Australia announced a joint project to develop underwater drone technology, part of their military alliance known as Aukus. The uncrewed undersea vehicle (UUV) technology is expected to be ready by next year and will focus on protecting seabed infrastructure, conducting surveillance, and bolstering deterrence in the Pacific, Atlantic, and High North regions.  The project aims to address concerns about threats to underwater cables and pipelines, which are increasingly vulnerable due to activities from Russia and China. The announcement comes amidst criticism of slow progress in Aukus projects, but the countries remain committed to their shared goal of strengthening defense capabilities.

articles.title: What’s gone wrong at Everyman and can the luxury cinema chain regain its magic? | Travel & leisure | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Everyman, the luxury cinema chain, is facing financial challenges after a quarter-century of success. The company issued a profit warning in December prompting investor concern and leading to the departure of its chief executive and finance director.  The company has struggled with rising competition from rivals like Odeon and Vue, as well as issues stemming from the pandemic and Hollywood strikes. Farah Golant, appointed interim chief executive, is tasked with turning around the business by focusing on paying down debt, optimizing food and beverage sales, and enhancing the membership program.  Analysts believe Everyman has a strong brand and potential to capitalize on the growing movie-going market, especially among younger generations.

articles.title: Europe airport chaos: UK travellers asked to arrive 3 hours early as border checks cause delays - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Passengers travelling between the UK and several European destinations are facing delays due to the European Union's Entry Exit System (EES), a new border management scheme requiring biometric data from non-EU travellers.  The system, which has recorded nearly 80 million entries and exits, is causing significant congestion at airports, particularly in Spain, Portugal, and France. Airlines, including Wizz Air, are advising passengers to arrive at least three hours before departure, while Airports Council International (ACI Europe) has called for improvements to border staffing levels and technical systems. Despite the challenges, the European Commission maintains that the system is largely functioning as intended.

articles.title: WHO chief visits epicentre of Ebola outbreak in DR Congo - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Tedros Adhanom Ghebreyesus, World Health Organization’s director general, visited the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to assess the Ebola outbreak response. The highly contagious haemorrhagic fever has already spread to three provinces in DRC and neighboring Uganda, with at least 1,077 suspected cases reported.  The WHO is working with the DRC government to address challenges and ensure community ownership of the response.  While a patient recovered from the outbreak on Wednesday, marking the first case discharged after two negative tests, medical experts are still insufficiently deployed to the region. The outbreak is occurring in an unstable area with limited laboratory capacity and ongoing conflict, raising concerns about its spread within displacement camps.

articles.title: Egypt warns Israel that dangerous Gaza escalations threaten ceasefire | Gaza News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Egypt has launched an urgent diplomatic intervention to salvage a fragile Gaza ceasefire agreement that is on the brink of collapse. Israel's recent military attacks and statements threatening to unravel months of diplomacy have pushed the deal to the edge.  The Egyptian government warned Israel against expanding its occupation in Gaza, while also inviting a senior Hamas delegation led by chief negotiator Khalil al-Hayya for urgent talks. The diplomatic moves come amid a surge in deadly air strikes that have killed at least 141 Palestinians in the last two weeks and an Israeli directive to expand control from 53% to 70%.  Egypt is coordinating with mediators in Qatar, Turkey, and the US to return the process to a negotiating track.

articles.title: UK urges Hajj pilgrims to leave Saudi Arabia before visa expiry, warns overstaying can lead to heavy fines | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: TOI World Desk, a team of seasoned journalists, provides global news and diverse perspectives to its readers. The organization is committed to accuracy, depth, and timeliness in delivering international affairs information.  TOI World Desk does not sell or share personal information for advertising purposes.

articles.title: KP CM Afridi urges GB chief justice to ensure transparency amid 'alarming' electoral environment - Pakistan - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Chief Minister Sohail Afridi urged the Chief Justice of the Supreme Appellate Court of Gilgit-Baltistan to intervene in upcoming elections due to reported incidents of harassment and restrictions on political activities.  Afridi cited the expulsion of PTI MNA Junaid Akbar and his team, as well as the alleged prevention of Asad Qaiser, a senior PTI leader, from reaching Islamabad airport, all during the campaign period. The CM emphasized constitutional guarantees for free and fair elections and called for swift action against any violations to ensure credible and transparent elections in Gilgit-Baltistan.

articles.title: The Iran war is dividing Muslims in the Philippines | US-Israel war on Iran | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: The US-Israeli war on Iran and the closure of the Strait of Hormuz have had a significant impact on Muslim communities in the Philippines, particularly in the Bangsamoro Autonomous Region.  Islamic scholars are divided over the conflict, with some supporting Iran's retaliation against the United States and others opposing it due to its Shia nature. This division has deepened existing tensions between scholars and fueled polarizing narratives about Palestine and the Israeli-Palestinian conflict. The entanglement of politics and religion in this context is further complicated by external influences from Arab countries and a lack of unity among Muslim communities.  This situation poses challenges for community cohesion, critical thinking, and the pursuit of self-determination.

articles.title: Sajid Javid says backing Liz Truss to lead Tories was his ‘biggest political mistake’ | Sajid Javid | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Sajid Javid, former chancellor, admitted his support for Liz Truss in the 2022 Conservative leadership contest was a "biggest mistake" in his political career. He stated that he no longer speaks with Truss and believes the quality of British politics has declined. He also argued for increased MP pay to attract high-caliber individuals, suggesting halving the number of MPs and doubling their salaries. Javid served as home secretary, chancellor, and health secretary under various prime ministers before resigning in 2022.  He is now a partner at Centricus, a private equity firm, and chair of the Holocaust Memorial Day Trust.

articles.title: Revival of Sabari rail project raises hopes in Central Travancore - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Sabari rail project, a key rail link connecting Kerala's eastern high ranges and improving access for Sabarimala pilgrims, is showing signs of revival.  After decades of uncertainty and delays, the State government is considering reopening land acquisition offices and resuming field survey work on the 70-km stretch of proposed alignment. The project has also received a boost with the Railways initiating steps to examine the feasibility of establishing a cargo terminal at the proposed Thodupuzha station.  This renewed activity follows the State Cabinet's decision earlier this year to bear 50% of the estimated cost of Rs.3,800 crore for land acquisition and project completion. The project was sanctioned in 1997-98 but faced prolonged disputes over cost sharing and alignment issues.

articles.title: Meet ICE agent Christian Castro, arrested in Texas for shooting at a Venezuelan in Minneapolis and lying about it - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: ICE agent Christian Castro has been arrested for shooting Julio Cesar Sosa-Celis, a Venezuelan migrant, during an incident in Minneapolis on January 14th. Castro initially claimed self-defense after a confrontation with Alfredo Aljorna, but surveillance footage contradicted his account.  The charges against both Aljorna and Sosa-Celis were dropped, and ICE officials are not supporting the state charges against Castro. The case is currently being handled at the federal level, with potential extradition proceedings to be determined by the states of Texas and Minnesota.

articles.title: 'US, Pakistan developing true friendship': Hegseth hails Islamabad's role in US-Iran negotiations - World - DAWN.COM
articles.rephrased_article: Pete Hegseth, Secretary of Defense, stated that a "true friendship" is developing between the United States and Pakistan as they collaborate on US-Iran peace negotiations.  He praised Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif and Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of the Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir for their role in these negotiations, highlighting the importance of this relationship. He acknowledged that both India and Pakistan are nuclear-capable countries and may develop ICBM threats but emphasized that the US is not pointing fingers at either country.  The US views Pakistan's collaboration on peace negotiations as beneficial to global stability.

articles.title: Israeli soldiers reach Nabatieh, one of southern Lebanon’s biggest cities | Israel attacks Lebanon News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Israel’s military has advanced beyond the Litani River in southern Lebanon for the first time since 2006, reaching the outskirts of Nabatieh. Hezbollah, a Shia militant group, is considered a key target by Israel, which issued evacuation orders for at least 10 villages. The Israeli army's Arabic spokesperson instructed residents to evacuate immediately, warning they could be killed if they remained.  The latest forced displacement orders are a further test to the nominal ceasefire in place since mid-April and are being met with concern from Lebanese officials.

articles.title: Anthropic’s alliance with pope on AI harms: all in good faith or ‘Vatican-washing?’ | AI (artificial intelligence) | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Pope Leo XIV delivered a warning about the dangers of artificial intelligence, highlighting its potential to replace workers and accelerate war. Anthropic co-founder Chris Olah, one of the leading figures in the AI industry, sat beside the Pope during the ceremony, raising questions about the potential for collaboration between the Catholic Church and the tech company.  Some experts argue that Anthropic's focus on safety and responsible AI use is a positive step, while others criticize the company for potentially prioritizing profit over ethical concerns. Dario Amodei, CEO of Anthropic, has acknowledged the risks associated with AI but also emphasized the need for financial support to develop the technology responsibly.  The Pope’s encyclical calls for more sustainable data centers, while Anthropic continues its ambitious plans to invest heavily in AI infrastructure.

articles.title: ‘That’s why we work in finance – so one day we can afford air-con’: Britain’s unequal heatwave | London | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: England experienced record-breaking temperatures this week, with London reaching 35C. While some residents in affluent areas like Canary Wharf enjoyed air-conditioned offices and homes, others in deprived areas faced extreme heat in their poorly insulated flats.  Asiyha, a resident of Whitechapel, struggled to sleep due to the high temperatures in her home. Toni, a tech worker, found relief in her newly built flat with air conditioning. Meanwhile, some residents relied on fans and other cooling methods like community gardens for respite from the heat.

articles.title: UK man, 68, dies rescuing granddaughter after family swept out to sea in Cornwall | World News - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Phil Crow, a 68-year-old grandfather, died while attempting to rescue his nine-year-old granddaughter, Sia Briskham, from rapidly changing sea conditions at Tregirls Beach in Cornwall, UK.  The incident occurred during a bank holiday weekend with unusually warm weather and saw Tina Crow, the granddaughter's mother, rescued by a passing boat and later checked by paramedics.  Sia was brought ashore by members of the public, while Mr Crow tragically succumbed to cardiac arrest despite efforts from emergency services including Coastguard teams, the Rock RNLI lifeboat crew, and Cornwall Air Ambulance.

articles.title: Rubio says Trump envoy Barrack to step down from Syria post | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Tom Barrack, the US Special Envoy for Syria, will step down from his formal post but remain in a key diplomatic role managing US policy in Syria and Iraq.  Marco Rubio, Secretary of State, announced this transition, highlighting Barrack's expertise and understanding of the "America First" agenda. While Barrack's special envoy title has expired, he will continue to coordinate these three areas of focus for the Trump administration. The move signals a desire for continuity in US policy towards Syria.

articles.title: Rise in youth unemployment driving more to homelessness, UK charities say | Young people | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Charities warn that a growing number of young people are becoming homeless or at risk of homelessness, with the youth unemployment rate reaching its highest point in over a decade. A government-commissioned review predicts a 25% rise in young people not in education, employment, or training (Neet) by early 2030s, and Centrepoint, a youth homelessness charity, reports that unstable housing is becoming increasingly common as the number of Neets surges.  Josh, a 23-year-old struggling to find work and secure stable housing, highlights the challenges young people face in securing employment and affordable housing, emphasizing the need for solutions that address both issues simultaneously. Lisa Doyle, head of policy at Centrepoint, emphasizes the scarcity of work opportunities for young people while acknowledging the role poverty plays in this crisis.

articles.title: Pakistan hires US lobbying firm to advance strategic interests in Washington amid Iran war diplomacy push - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: Pakistan has hired a US lobbying firm, Ervin Graves Strategy Group, led by former Republican Congressman Tom Graves, for a two-year contract. The agreement aims to advance Pakistan's diplomatic, economic and strategic interests in Washington, D.C., including monitoring legislative developments and engaging with key stakeholders. The firm will also work to expand Pakistan's engagement with US media and facilitate visits from US lawmakers to Pakistan. This move comes amidst Pakistan's efforts to mediate between Tehran and Washington.

articles.title: What Hegseth’s comments at Shangri-La Dialogue say about US foreign policy | Politics News | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Pete Hegseth, the US Defense Secretary, addressed key foreign policy issues at the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore. He expressed concern over China's growing military presence and urged allies to increase defense spending to counter its influence. He also discussed Taiwan, stating that while US commitment to the island remains, President Donald Trump will ultimately decide on any arms sales.  Hegseth emphasized the need for partnerships rather than relying on US military power and warned of potential US attacks on Iran if a satisfactory deal is not reached with Tehran.

articles.title: ‘Maybe it’s because we love the sesh’: how Wales is bucking Britain’s pub-closing trend | Wales | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: Despite a national trend of pub closures, the Pig & Swill in Cardiff has seen success since opening.  The new taphouse, co-founded by Lewis Dwyer and Andy Aston, is attracting customers with its focus on quality local produce and its location near popular attractions like Victoria Park. While Wales has bucked the national trend with new pub openings, the hospitality industry overall remains under pressure from rising costs and taxes. David Chapman, executive director of UK Hospitality Cymru, calls for government action to support businesses in the sector.

articles.title: Congress govt. in Himachal changing election rules to hijack local body polls: BJP State chief - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: Rajeev Bindal, BJP Himachal Pradesh President, accused the Congress government of attempting to manipulate urban local body and Panchayati Raj elections in the state. He claimed that the government amended election rules, granting deputy commissioners discretionary authority over meeting timings, and delaying the elections. Bindal argued this is an attempt to gain control over municipal councils and other bodies through political influence and money power, violating democratic principles and electoral laws.

articles.title: Unruly passenger disrupts United Airlines flight bound for Minneapolis, plane seeks FBI's help - The Times of India
articles.rephrased_article: United Airlines flight UA2005, en route to Minneapolis from Chicago, was diverted to Dane County Regional Airport in Wisconsin after an unruly passenger attempted to enter the cockpit.  The FBI and local law enforcement responded to the incident, detaining the disruptive passenger who was eventually secured by authorities. The plane landed safely in Madison and passengers resumed their journey to Minneapolis without injuries.

articles.title: North Korean POWs: Political pawns in Russia’s war on Ukraine? | Kim Jong Un | Al Jazeera
articles.rephrased_article: Volodymyr Zelenskyy announced the capture of two North Korean soldiers in January 2025, marking the first evidence of Kim Jong Un's secret deployment of 15,000 special forces to support Russia's invasion of Ukraine. International human rights organizations are concerned that publicizing the POWs' images and their imprisonment violates the Geneva Convention and puts them and their families in North Korea at risk.  The challenges of bringing these soldiers to safety in South Korea remain a significant issue.

articles.title: Why $1bn in Balkans energy contracts are going to an obscure company connected to Donald Trump | Bosnia and Herzegovina | The Guardian
articles.rephrased_article: AAFS Infrastructure and Energy, a company with ties to Donald Trump's associates, is close to securing a $1 billion contract to build a pipeline across the Balkans. The project aims to replace Russian gas supplies with US-sourced natural gas, but its path forward has been complicated by concerns over corruption, potential political interference, and the involvement of ultranationalist leader Milorad Dodik.  The Trump administration is pushing for the project's completion, despite warnings from international organizations about transparency and potential risks to Bosnia's peace agreement. The company's executives have connections to Donald Trump Jr., Jesse Binnall, and Michael Flynn, who previously worked on efforts to overturn the 2020 presidential election results.  The pipeline's construction could significantly impact energy security in the region, but its success hinges on navigating complex political dynamics and securing approval from all stakeholders.

articles.title: F&O Talk: Nifty may stay range-bound; Sudeep Shah sees opportunities in banks, IT, picks 7 stocks - The Economic Times
articles.rephrased_article: The Sensex and Nifty 50 experienced significant losses, dropping over 1,092 points and nearly 359 points respectively. This volatility was driven by a surge in the India VIX, indicating heightened market uncertainty. Analyst Sudeep Shah highlighted concerns about Nifty rollover, suggesting potential profit-taking or cautiousness near higher levels. He also noted that Bank Nifty rollover declined sharply, raising questions about its future performance. Foreign Institutional Investors (FIIs) exhibited mixed sentiment, with short positions being reduced but long positions increasing. Despite the market's volatility, some sectors like private banks and PSU banks are showing strength.

articles.title: Likely moderation in economic activity, near-term growth outlook shows cautious resilience: Finance Ministry - The Hindu
articles.rephrased_article: The Finance Ministry of India reported that the near-term outlook for the Indian economy is one of cautious resilience, despite forecasts of a below-normal monsoon and moderation in economic activity.
